title: Forward Deployed Engineer
summary: Forward deployed engineers work closely with one customer at a time, using code, data pipelines and their company's platform to solve that customer's real problems. It suits strong programmers who also like talking to people and owning outcomes.

sources.title: A Day in the Life of a Palantir Forward Deployed Software Engineer – Palantir Blog
Dev versus Delta: Demystifying engineering roles at Palantir – Palantir Blog

nodes.title: Python programming
nodes.summary: Learn Python well: data types, functions, classes, modules, errors and virtual environments. FDE work ranges from software development to data engineering, and Python is a practical language for both.
nodes.proof: A command-line tool in Python, with tests, that reads a CSV file and produces a clean summary report.

sources.title: A Day in the Life of a Palantir Forward Deployed Software Engineer – Palantir Blog

nodes.title: SQL and relational databases
nodes.summary: Customer data usually lives in databases. Learn to create tables, query, join, aggregate and update data, and understand transactions and window functions. The PostgreSQL tutorial covers all of these for free.
nodes.proof: A small PostgreSQL database for a made-up shop with 10 SQL queries (joins, aggregates, a window function) and their answers.

nodes.title: Data cleaning and pipelines
nodes.summary: Real customer data is messy. Learn to load, clean, reshape, merge and summarise data with pandas, then turn the steps into a repeatable script. This is the data engineering side of the role.
nodes.proof: A script that takes two messy public datasets, cleans and joins them, and writes the result to a database table.

sources.title: Dev versus Delta: Demystifying engineering roles at Palantir – Palantir Blog

nodes.title: Web apps and APIs
nodes.summary: FDEs often build tools and workflows that customers use. Learn JavaScript, how to build and call REST APIs, and enough front end to make a simple, usable interface on top of your data.

resources.title: Learn web development – MDN Web Docs

nodes.proof: A small web app with a REST API and a page that lets a user search and filter records from your database.

sources.title: A Day in the Life of a Palantir Forward Deployed Software Engineer – Palantir Blog

nodes.title: Deployment with Docker
nodes.summary: Your code has to run on someone else's systems, not just your laptop. Learn to package apps in containers, run multi-container setups with Compose, and keep production systems monitored and maintained.

resources.title: Overview of the Docker workshop – Docker Docs

nodes.proof: Your web app and its database running together with one docker compose command, with setup steps in the README.

sources.title: How to Become a Full Stack Developer – roadmap.sh
A Day in the Life of a Palantir Forward Deployed Software Engineer – Palantir Blog

nodes.title: Using AI models in applications
nodes.summary: Many companies now hire FDEs to put AI into customers' workflows. Learn to apply pre-trained models: prompting, embeddings, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and simple agents, plus their limits and safety.
nodes.proof: A small RAG app that answers questions over a set of public documents and shows which passages it used.

nodes.title: Working with customers
nodes.summary: The role is 'one customer, many capabilities': you learn the customer's problem, decide what to build, explain trade-offs plainly and send field lessons back to the product team. Practise this with real users.

resources.title: Dev versus Delta: Demystifying engineering roles at Palantir – Palantir Blog
A Day in the Life of a Palantir Forward Deployed Software Engineer – Palantir Blog

nodes.proof: Interview a college office or local shop about one data problem and write a one-page brief of the problem and your proposed fix.

sources.title: Dev versus Delta: Demystifying engineering roles at Palantir – Palantir Blog

nodes.title: End-to-end project for a real user
nodes.summary: Build one project for an actual person or group: collect their data, clean it, build a tool on top (optionally with AI), deploy it and improve it from their feedback. This shows the whole FDE loop.

resources.title: Build and share a containerized application – Docker Docs

nodes.proof: A deployed tool used by at least one real user, with a README covering the problem, design, data pipeline and what you changed after feedback.

nodes.title: Interview prep and job search
nodes.summary: Practise coding problems, system design and explaining your end-to-end project to a non-technical person. Read companies' own interview advice, and apply to FDE roles as well as backend and data engineering roles.

nodes.proof: Two mock interviews: one coding or system design round, and one where you explain your project to someone outside tech.
